4. How do you spell your name?
Complete the conversations. Then role-play them with a partner.
Project: Learn how to use a dictionary.
Section B, Activity 2a. Read the dictionary pages. Circle the words in blue. What order are they in?
asleep: sleeping. The baby is asleep, so we have to be quiet.
astronaut: a person who works in space.
at: He gets up at seven o'clock. Let's meet at the school gate.
aunt: your mother's or father's sister.
autumn: the time of the year between summer and winter.
away: to another place. The mouse ran away when it saw the cat.
awful: bad, terrible. The pain was awful.
axe: You use an axe to cut wood or trees.
baby: a very young child. Babies.
back, one: the part behind. Is your back still painful?
back, two: to where it was before. Give me the book back.
bad: not good. A rainy day is a bad day for a picnic.
bag: A bag is used to carry things.
ball: something round to play with.
balloon: a toy made of rubber that you blow up.
bank, one: a side of a river.
bank, two: a place to keep money in safely.
Section B, Activity 2b. Number the following words in alphabetical order.
you, English, speak, after, bike, cold, hello, morning, please, come, what, goodbye, spell, afternoon, evening.
Section B, Activity 2c. Have a competition. Find these words in a dictionary as fast as you can.
